reasoning: In March 2016, Google DeepMind's AlphaGo played a five-game match in Seoul against South Korean Go grandmaster Lee Sedol, winning 4 games to 1. Lee Sedol, who won 18 international titles, was widely regarded as the premier Go player of the era. Prior to the match, AI experts widely believed that a computer program defeating a top human Go champion was at least a decade away due to the immense complexity and intuition required for Go.
